newsitem.title: USA: FBI says agents to stay in Saudi Arabia.
newsitem.headline: FBI says agents to stay in Saudi Arabia.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation denied a news report on Saturday that it is pulling its agents out of Saudi Arabia because of unhappiness with Saudi cooperation in its investigation of the June 25 truck bombing that killed 19 U.S. servicemen.
"Reports that the FBI is withdrawing its agents out of Saudi Arabia because of dissatisfaction with the level of cooperation by the Saudi government are not true," it said in a brief statement.
The New York Times reported on Saturday that FBI Director Louis Freeh had pulled a team of FBI agents out of Saudi Arabia in what appeared to be a threat to end U.S. involvement in the investigation.
But the FBI statement said agents on temporary duty in Saudi Arabia "are being continuously rotated home in the normal course for work and personal reasons."

"Contrary to media reports reflecting speculation by unnamed sources, agents remain in Saudi Arabia to continue working with Saudi law enforcemnt authorities on the bombing investigation," the FBI said.
It said the FBI also has a temporary legal attache office in Saudi Arabia and that Freeh had selected a permanent legal attache and assistant who are to arrive in the next 60 days.
Defense Secretary William Perry said on Friday that the United States has not found a culprit for the bomb attack.

When asked about a Washington Post report that Saudi Arabia had arrested 40 people and pinned partial blame on Iran, Perry told reporters: "We have reached no conclusions about who was responsible for this."
